sections.title: Put past events in order
body: A list becomes a story when the listener knows when things happened and in what order. Start with a time: igår (yesterday), igår kväll (last night), i morse (this morning), i lördags (last Saturday), förra veckan (last week), förra året (last year). Then guide the listener with först (first), sedan (then), efter det (after that) and till slut (finally). In speech, sedan is often said sen.

Swedish keeps the verb in the second position. When a time phrase or a signpost takes the first place, the past-tense verb comes next and the subject follows: Förra veckan läste vi en bok. English says “Last week we read”, so English speakers often write Förra veckan vi läste. That is the most common mistake here. Put the verb straight after the first phrase.
To say ago, wrap the time between för and sedan: för en månad sedan (a month ago), för två dagar sedan (two days ago). English puts ago only at the end; Swedish needs both words.

Började works like a modal verb: the next verb stays in the infinitive. Jag började skriva. Jag började att skriva is also correct. Att before an action means to: Jag gillar att dansa. Before a whole statement it means that: Jag berättade att jag var trött.

examples.en: Yesterday I played video games.
examples.note: Igår first; spelade second; jag third.

examples.fi: Igår kväll beställde jag en pizza.
examples.en: Last night I ordered a pizza.
examples.note: The whole time phrase igår kväll fills the first place.

examples.fi: Först åt jag fattiga riddare till frukost. Sedan gick jag på bio. Efter det träffade jag en vän.
examples.en: First I ate French toast for breakfast. Then I went to the cinema. After that I met a friend.
examples.note: Three signposts make the order clear. Fattiga riddare (poor knights) is the Swedish name for French toast.

examples.fi: Jag reste till Spanien för ett år sedan.
examples.en: I travelled to Spain a year ago.
She bought a cake yesterday (a cake, not bread).
examples.note: The teacher also starts with an object, the thing the action affects, to stress it. The verb still comes second.

sections.memoryTip: TIME → VERB → PERSON: Förra veckan → läste → vi. The verb never waits in third place.
sections.tryIt: Say three true or invented events from yesterday. Begin each line with Igår, Sedan or Efter det, and put the verb next.

activity.label: Verb second?
activity.title: Is the verb in the second place?
activity.instructions: Read each line and predict: is it correct Swedish, or does the verb come too late? Then say the correct version aloud.

items.why: Igår takes the first place, so the verb comes next: Igår spelade jag datorspel.

items.fi: Förra veckan läste vi en bok.
items.en: Last week we read a book.
items.why: Förra veckan, then läste, then vi.

items.en: Then we went to the cinema.
items.why: Sedan is a signpost in the first place: Sedan gick vi på bio.

items.fi: Igår kväll beställde jag en pizza.
items.en: Last night I ordered a pizza.
items.why: Igår kväll is one time phrase, so beställde is still second.

items.fi: Jag reste till Spanien förra året.
items.en: I travelled to Spain last year.
items.why: The subject jag is first, so reste is second. The time can also come at the end.

items.fi: I morse jag tränade på gymmet.
items.en: This morning I worked out at the gym.
items.why: After I morse the verb comes next: I morse tränade jag på gymmet.
The object en kaka is first, and köpte is still second.
Till slut takes the first place: Till slut gick jag hem.

activity.summary: Whatever comes first, the verb comes next.

sections.title: Write to a friend
body: An informal letter or message sounds like a conversation. It has four parts: a greeting with your friend's name (Hej Elin!), your news in time order, one real question so your friend can answer, and a warm closing such as Kram, Vi ses or Vi hörs, with your name.
After the greeting, a short friendly question is natural: Hur är det med dig? or Hur mår du? Then tell your news with time words and signposts. Short and correct is better than long and unsure.

A diary is for yourself and a letter is for another person, but both often begin with a date: den 4 maj. Read it aloud with an ordinal number, a counting word for order: den fjärde maj. You will practise more ordinals in Lecture 10.
The YKI basic-level writing test has this kind of task: a short card or message to a friend, with a list of points to cover. You must open and close it in a suitable way and cover every point.

examples.en: Hi Elin!
How are things with you?
examples.note: A friendly start before your news.

examples.fi: I måndags började jag en ny kurs. Sedan träffade jag en vän.
examples.en: On Monday I started a new course. Then I met a friend.
examples.note: Two pieces of news in time order.

examples.en: How was your week?
Hugs, Alex

sections.title: Say what it is about
body: Use handlar om to name the topic of a book, film, letter or conversation: Filmen handlar om vänskap. Learn it as one chunk.
Do not translate English word for word. Swedish does not say Filmen är om vänskap. Say Filmen handlar om vänskap.
In a question, om moves to the end: Vad handlar filmen om? (What is the film about?)
Without om, handla is a different verb: it means to shop. Vi handlade mat means We bought food. Listen for om to know which one you hear.

examples.en: The film is about friendship.
The book is about Finland.
What is the book about?
examples.note: In a question, om goes to the end.

examples.fi: Jag har något viktigt att berätta. Det handlar om jobbet.
examples.en: I have something important to tell you. It is about work.
examples.note: A useful way to start news in a letter.

examples.en: On Saturday we bought food.
examples.note: No om: handla means to shop.

sections.memoryTip: THING + handlar om + TOPIC. Question: Vad handlar den om? No om = shopping.
sections.tryIt: Name one film or book you like and say what it is about. Then ask: Vad handlar din favoritfilm om?

activity.label: About or shopping?
activity.title: Which handla is it?
activity.instructions: Decide what handlar means in each line. Look for om. Then say the line aloud.

items.fi: Filmen handlar om två gamla vänner.
items.why: Handlar om + topic: the film is about two old friends.
No om after handlade, and mat is what they bought.
Om sits at the end of the question: What is the letter about?

items.fi: Jag handlar i en mataffär nära jobbet.
items.why: I en mataffär tells where you shop: I shop at a grocery shop near work.
Handlar om + Finland: the book is about Finland.
No om after handlade, and kläder is what she bought.

activity.summary: Handlar om + topic means is about. Handla without om means to shop.

sections.title: Small words after verbs
body: Some Swedish verbs and adjectives always take a small word after them, a preposition. It is often not the one English uses, so learn the pair as one chunk.
Waiting and many feelings take på: vänta på (wait for), arg på (angry with), besviken på (disappointed in). Being in love takes i: kär i.
Berätta has two partners: berätta om something (tell about it) and berätta för someone (tell it to them): Jag berättade om helgen för Elin.

examples.fi: Jag väntade på bussen i tjugo minuter.
examples.en: I waited for the bus for twenty minutes.
Do not be angry with me!
I was disappointed in the film.
Elin is in love with Mikko.

examples.fi: Jag berättade om helgen för Elin.
examples.en: I told Elin about the weekend.
examples.note: om = about; för = to the person.

sections.memoryTip: English for, with, in → Swedish often på: vänta på, arg på, besviken på.
sections.tryIt: Say one true sentence with vänta på and one with berätta för.

activity.instructions: Match each English phrase with its Swedish partner. Then say each pair aloud.
activity.pattern: English for, with and in often become på in Swedish. Learn each verb with its partner.

reading_passage.text:
Hej Maja!
I måndags började jag en kvällskurs i indisk matlagning. Först träffade jag läraren och de andra deltagarna. Sedan lagade vi en linsgryta tillsammans. Efter kursen drack vi te. Kursen handlar om mat från Indien, så nu kan jag laga mat till Alex! Vad gjorde du i måndags?
Kram, Elin

To invite Maja to the cinema

writing.prompt: Write an informal message to a friend about your week.
writing.situation: Your friend Elin writes: “Hej! Hur var din vecka? Vad gjorde du?” (Hi! How was your week? What did you do?) Write back. As in the YKI basic-level test, open and close the message in a suitable way and cover every point.
points: Greet Elin and ask how she is.
Tell at least two things you did this week, in order.
Ask Elin one question about her week.
writing.help: Hej Elin! · Hur är det med dig? · I måndags … · Först … · Sedan … · Efter det … · Det var … · Vad gjorde du i helgen? · Kram, …
writing.model:
Hej Elin!
Hur är det med dig? Min vecka var bra. I måndags tränade jag på gymmet. Sedan träffade jag en vän och vi drack kaffe tillsammans. I onsdags såg jag en film hemma. Den handlar om en hund. Det var mysigt! Vad gjorde du i helgen?
Kram,
Alex

route.expectedOutput: Tell a friend about last weekend in five to seven lines, then write a 40–70-word informal letter about your week.
route.transferPrompt: Tell it again, but change one event or add how you felt.
route.returnPrompt: Without notes, tell three events from last weekend in order.
successChecks: I say when the events happened.
I put the verb second after a time word: Igår åt jag …
I connect events with först, sedan or efter det.
My letter has a greeting, news, a question and a closing.

checkpoint.prompt: Produce: “Last week we read a book.”
answers: Förra veckan läste vi en bok.
Vi läste en bok förra veckan.
checkpoint.hint: Time first, verb second, then the subject.
checkpoint.explanation: Förra veckan läste vi en bok. Förra veckan takes the first place, so läste comes before vi. Vi läste en bok förra veckan is also correct.

checkpoint.prompt: Choose the line with correct word order.
answers: Igår spelade jag datorspel.
checkpoint.hint: After Igår, put the verb before the subject.
checkpoint.explanation: Igår spelade jag … keeps the verb second.

answers: handlar om
checkpoint.hint: Use the chunk for saying the topic of a film or book.
checkpoint.explanation: Filmen handlar om vänskap: The film is about friendship. Swedish does not say är om.

checkpoint.prompt: Produce: “Two days ago I ordered a pizza.”
answers: För två dagar sedan beställde jag en pizza.
För två dagar sen beställde jag en pizza.
Jag beställde en pizza för två dagar sen.
Jag beställde en pizza för två dagar sedan.
checkpoint.hint: Wrap the time with för … sedan. If it comes first, the verb comes next.
checkpoint.explanation: För två dagar sedan beställde jag en pizza. Jag beställde en pizza för två dagar sedan is also correct.

answers: på
checkpoint.hint: Angry with: Swedish uses a different small word.
checkpoint.explanation: Arg på: Bli inte arg på mig! (Do not be angry with me!)

checkpoint.prompt: Which ending is warm and informal?
answers: Kram, Elin

assignment.title: Episode 8 mission: My weekend in order
assignment.instructions:
CORE: Tell a friend about last weekend in five to seven lines. Say when, and connect at least three events with först, sedan, efter det or till slut. Finish with how it was.

WRITE: Answer a friend in 40–70 words. Include a greeting, two events, one question and an informal closing.

DIARY: Keep your daily diary (5–10 minutes). Today, start three sentences with a time phrase and use för … sedan once.

RETURN: Tomorrow, tell three events again without looking.
assignment.model: I helgen träffade jag en vän. Först drack vi kaffe. Sedan gick vi på bio. Efter det åt vi middag tillsammans. Till slut gick jag hem. Det var en rolig helg.

takeaways: A time phrase can come first: Förra veckan läste vi en bok. The verb still comes second.
Order a past story with först, sedan, efter det and till slut. Ago is för … sedan.
Det handlar om tells the topic. In a question: Vad handlar den om? Without om, handla means to shop.
Learn verbs with their small word: vänta på, arg på, besviken på, berätta för.
A friendly letter has a greeting, news, a question and a warm closing.
